title: Your first conversation
chapter: Part I — Getting started (new chapter after ch.16)
scenario: It is your first day with AgentBridge. You do not need to know anything about AI. You just open the window and type what you would tell a new assistant.
command: Hello! What can you help me with in my office?
caption: The AgentBridge terminal window, ready for your first message
result: The agent answers in plain words and lists what it can do: write documents, build spreadsheets, read and send email, research the web, make presentations and more. You keep talking to it like a person. Everything happens in this one window.
tip: You never have to memorise anything. Press F1 at any time for help, and the bottom bar always shows what is active.

title: Turn the right tools on
chapter: Part I — Getting started (new chapter after ch.16)
scenario: Your assistant starts light and quick. When you need a special skill — like making a real Excel file — you switch that tool on for the conversation.
command: /tools
caption: The tools checklist: tick what the agent may use
result: A simple checklist appears. You move with the arrow keys and tick a tool with the Space bar. Your choice is remembered, so next time the tool is already there. The core tools (files, history, scheduling) are always on.
tip: In a hurry? Type the name of a ready-made set, like /tools spreadsheet-files, and it is switched on in one step.

title: Choose which AI answers you
chapter: Part I — Getting started (new chapter after ch.16)
scenario: You can use a big AI in the cloud or a private one on your own computer. Switching between them takes a few seconds and changes nothing else.
command: /model
caption: The Model setup window: pick your AI provider and model
result: You see your providers and the active model. Pick another one and the whole conversation continues with it. Your documents, tools and history stay exactly where they are — only the answering AI changes.
tip: A local model keeps your data on your own machine. A cloud model is usually sharper. You decide per conversation.

title: Every command in one place
chapter: Part I — Getting started (new chapter after ch.16)
scenario: You forgot how to upload a file. Instead of searching the internet, you open the built-in help and read the short list.
command: F1
caption: The help screen lists every command with a one-line explanation
result: The help screen shows the commands and what each one does: /files to upload, /model to switch AI, /email to set up mail, and more. It closes with one key. No manuals, no googling.
tip: Typing / opens a live list that filters as you type, so you often do not need the full help screen at all.

title: Give the agent a document to read
chapter: Part I — Getting started (new chapter after ch.16)
scenario: You want the agent to work with a file you already have — a supplier list, a contract draft, a report. You attach it to the chat.
command: @  (then pick the file)
caption: The @ palette: choose an uploaded file to attach to your message
result: The file is attached to your message. The agent reads it and answers using its real contents — summarising it, checking it, or building something new from it. Nothing leaves your machine except what you choose to send to the AI.
tip: You can attach several files at once. The agent keeps them for the conversation, so you can ask follow-up questions.

title: Make an invoice in seconds
scenario: You finished a job for a client and need a clean invoice. Normally you open a template, type the lines, fix the totals. Today you just ask.
command: Make an invoice for Bright Cafe for 12 hours of bookkeeping at 45 euros an hour, due in 14 days.
caption: A finished invoice document produced by the agent
result: The agent writes a proper invoice with your business details, the line items, the subtotal, tax and total, and a due date. You get a real document you can print or send. If a number is wrong, you say so and it fixes it.
tip: Ask for it as a real Word file (/tools office-files) if you want to keep editing it in Microsoft Office.

title: Draft a service contract
scenario: A new client wants everything in writing before starting. You need a simple contract that covers the work, the price and the dates.
command: Draft a service contract between my studio and a client for a 3-month website project at 6,000 euros, with a 50% deposit.
caption: A drafted service agreement, ready for review
result: The agent produces a clear contract with the parties, the scope of work, the payment schedule, and the timeline. It is a starting point you can review and adjust — not legal advice, but a solid draft that saves you hours of blank-page work.
tip: Attach your old contract and ask it to follow the same style and clauses.

title: Write a formal letter
scenario: You need to send a formal letter — to a landlord, a supplier, a bank. Getting the tone and format right takes time.
command: Write a formal letter to our landlord asking to renew the lease for another two years on the same terms.
caption: A formal business letter, formatted and ready
result: The agent writes the letter with the right greeting, a clear body and a polite closing, in your business voice. You review it, change a word if you like, and send it.
tip: Tell it who you are writing to and what you want; it handles the formal tone for you.

title: Turn an idea into a proposal
scenario: A potential client asked for a written proposal. You have the ideas in your head but no time to lay them out.
command: Create a project proposal for a small online shop: goals, what we deliver, timeline of 8 weeks, and a price of 9,500 euros.
caption: A structured project proposal document
result: The agent builds a proposal with the client's goal, your solution, the deliverables, the timeline and the price — all in a clean layout that looks like it took a whole afternoon. It took a minute.
tip: Add your logo and a sentence about past results to make it feel personal.

title: Clean meeting notes
scenario: You jotted rough notes during a meeting. Now someone needs clean minutes with the decisions and who does what.
command: Turn these rough notes into clean meeting minutes with a decisions list and action items: [paste notes]
caption: Tidy meeting minutes with decisions and actions
result: The agent turns your messy notes into structured minutes: what was discussed, what was decided, and an action list with owners. You can send them straight to the team.
tip: Paste your notes as they are — the agent sorts the order and the wording.

title: A simple staff handbook
scenario: Your small team keeps asking the same questions. A short handbook answers them once, for everyone.
command: Write a short employee handbook covering working hours, holidays, remote work rules and who to ask for help.
caption: A friendly staff handbook, ready to share
result: The agent writes a clear, friendly handbook in plain language, with each topic on its own page. Update it any time by asking — 'add a line about the new parking rule'.
tip: Keep it in your documents area so the agent can answer questions from it later.

title: A budget you can read
scenario: You want to see planned versus actual spending for the month, with a chart, without fighting a spreadsheet for an hour.
command: Build a monthly budget spreadsheet with planned and actual for rent, marketing and salaries, plus a chart.
caption: A budget spreadsheet with a clear bar chart
result: The agent creates the spreadsheet with the categories, the planned and actual columns, totals, and a chart that shows the difference at a glance. You can open it in Excel and keep working.
tip: Ask for the chart title and the currency so it matches your business.

title: Track your sales
scenario: You want one sheet that shows sales by month and where they came from, so you can spot what is working.
command: Create a sales tracker with month, channel and revenue, and a chart of revenue by channel.
caption: A sales tracker with revenue by channel
result: The agent builds the tracker and the chart. Add rows as you go, or attach your raw sales list and ask it to fill the sheet for you.
tip: Attach a messy export from your shop and say 'clean this into a tracker' — it will.

title: Keep stock in order
scenario: You need a simple stock list with quantities and reorder levels, so nothing runs out unnoticed.
command: Make an inventory spreadsheet with item, quantity, reorder level and supplier, and highlight what is below the reorder level.
caption: An inventory sheet with low-stock items highlighted
result: The agent sets up the inventory sheet and marks the items that need reordering. Update the quantities and ask it to re-check any time.
tip: A weekly scheduled check can tell you what to reorder before you run out.

title: Your key numbers on one sheet
scenario: You want the few numbers that matter — revenue, customers, costs — together, with a chart you can show your team.
command: Build a small KPI dashboard: monthly revenue, new customers, cost, and a chart of revenue trend.
caption: A KPI dashboard with the numbers that matter
result: The agent lays out the key figures and a trend chart on one clean sheet. It becomes the page you look at every week.
tip: Keep the same sheet updated and ask the agent to compare this month to last month.

title: A weekly timesheet
scenario: You need to log hours per person per project for billing, in a tidy weekly grid.
command: Create a weekly timesheet with people, projects, hours per day and a total per person.
caption: A weekly timesheet with totals per person
result: The agent builds the timesheet grid with daily columns and automatic totals. Fill it in or attach your rough hours and let it sort them.
tip: Multiply hours by each rate and you have a billing sheet too — just ask.

title: A pitch deck from one prompt
scenario: You have ten minutes to pitch your idea and no slides. You describe the story and the agent builds the deck.
command: Make a 6-slide pitch deck for my delivery startup: problem, solution, market, model, traction, ask.
caption: A presentation slide built by the agent
result: The agent designs the slides with a clean look, one clear idea per slide, and the right order for a pitch. In the browser you press F11 for full screen and present.
tip: Need a real .pptx to send? Use /tools office-files and ask for PowerPoint.

title: A client sales deck
scenario: Before a client meeting you want a deck that shows what you did for them and what comes next.
command: Create a sales deck summarising our work with Acme and proposing the next phase.
caption: A client-facing sales presentation slide
result: The agent builds a focused deck: results so far, what the client gained, and the proposed next step. You tweak the numbers and present with confidence.
tip: Attach the project report and the agent pulls the highlights into the slides.

title: Train your team fast
scenario: You need to teach your team a new process. A clear slide deck makes the training short and consistent.
command: Make a training deck on how to handle a customer refund, step by step.
caption: A step-by-step training slide
result: The agent turns the process into clear slides, one step each, easy to follow. Use it for onboarding and refreshers.
tip: Add a final slide with 'who to ask' so people know where to get help.

title: A quarterly board review
scenario: The quarterly review needs the numbers and the plan in a tidy deck. You have the data, not the time.
command: Build a quarterly review deck: results, highlights, challenges, and next quarter plan.
caption: A quarterly review presentation slide
result: The agent assembles the review deck with the results, the wins, the issues and the plan — laid out so the meeting moves quickly.
tip: Attach your KPI sheet and the agent puts the charts in the slides.

title: A market analysis report
chapter: Ch.12 Where AI can help your business
scenario: You are thinking of a new product line and want a serious look at the market, with sources, as a PDF.
command: Produce a PDF market analysis of the specialty coffee retail segment: size, trends, competitors and outlook.
caption: A detailed PDF report with charts and sources
result: The agent researches the topic and writes a structured PDF report with sections, figures and cited sources — the kind of document that normally takes a consultant days.
tip: Tell it the depth you need. 'Short brief' or 'detailed report' changes the length.

title: A financial summary report
scenario: Your accountant asked for a clean summary of the year. You want it as a proper PDF.
command: Create a PDF financial summary for 2025: revenue, costs, profit and a year-over-year chart.
caption: A financial summary PDF with charts
result: The agent builds the report with the figures, the trend chart and a plain-language summary of what the numbers mean.
tip: Attach your ledger export and the agent reads the real numbers into the report.

title: Research, written up
chapter: Ch.12 Where AI can help your business
scenario: You needed answers to a business question and a document to share. Research plus write-up, in one go.
command: Research the best ways for a small bakery to take orders online and write a PDF report with the options and a recommendation.
caption: A research report PDF with options and a recommendation
result: The agent searches the web, weighs the options and writes a clear report ending with a practical recommendation you can act on.
tip: Ask it to list the sources so you can check anything yourself.

title: Answer an email in your voice
scenario: A customer email needs a warm, clear reply. You tell the agent the gist; it writes the message.
command: Reply to this customer thanking them and confirming we will ship tomorrow: [paste email]
caption: A drafted email reply, ready to send
result: The agent writes a friendly, professional reply that sounds like you. You read it once, press send, and move on.
tip: Set up your mail once with /email. After that, reading and sending work from the chat.

title: A polite follow-up
scenario: A client has not answered your quote. A short, friendly follow-up keeps it moving without being pushy.
command: Write a short follow-up to a client who has not replied to our quote from last week.
caption: A friendly follow-up email draft
result: The agent writes a light, polite nudge that reminds without pressure. You send it and keep the relationship warm.
tip: A scheduled follow-up can send these for you if a reply has not arrived.

title: Send the invoice by email
scenario: You made the invoice and now it needs to reach the client with a short, clear message.
command: Email the invoice we just made to the client with a short, friendly cover note.
caption: The invoice attached to a ready-to-send email
result: The agent attaches the invoice and writes a short cover note with the amount and due date. One message, sent.
tip: Chain it: 'make the invoice and email it to the client' in a single ask.

title: A customer newsletter
scenario: You want to keep customers informed with a monthly update, but writing it every month is a chore.
command: Write a monthly newsletter for our customers: new items, a tip, and a small discount code.
caption: A newsletter draft ready to send
result: The agent writes the newsletter in your voice with the news, a useful tip and the offer. Send it, or let it prepare one on a schedule.
tip: A monthly scheduled task can draft the newsletter for your review each time.

title: Catch up on your inbox
scenario: You were away and the inbox piled up. You want the short version: what needs you now.
command: Summarise my unread emails and tell me which ones need a reply today.
caption: A short summary of the inbox with the urgent items
result: The agent reads your unread mail and gives you a short list: what is urgent, what can wait, and what you can ignore. You tackle the real priorities first.
tip: A morning summary can be scheduled so this is waiting for you with your coffee.

title: Know your competitors
chapter: Ch.12 Where AI can help your business
scenario: You want to know what three competitors are charging and how they position themselves.
command: Look up our three main competitors and summarise their prices and what they highlight.
caption: A browser view of the agent's research findings
result: The agent browses the competitors' pages and brings back a clear comparison of prices and positioning, with the links so you can check.
tip: Ask for it as a document or a spreadsheet if you want to keep the comparison.

title: What is trending in your field
chapter: Ch.12 Where AI can help your business
scenario: You want to stay current without reading dozens of articles. You ask for the trends that matter.
command: What are the top three trends in small-business e-commerce this year? Give me sources.
caption: A research summary with sources
result: The agent searches recent articles and gives you the key trends in plain language, each with a source you can open.
tip: A weekly trend digest can be scheduled to keep you current automatically.

title: Check a supplier before you commit
chapter: Ch.19 Connecting AI to systems you already use
scenario: Before signing with a new supplier you want a quick background check.
command: Research this supplier and tell me their reputation, how long they have been around, and any red flags.
caption: A due-diligence summary of a supplier
result: The agent gathers what is publicly available and gives you a balanced picture with sources, so you decide with your eyes open.
tip: Ask it to list what it could not find, so you know where to dig further.

title: Your industry news, summarised
chapter: Ch.12 Where AI can help your business
scenario: You want the day's relevant news without spending an hour on news sites.
command: Give me a short digest of today's news that matters to a small logistics business.
caption: A short news digest with links
result: The agent scans the news and writes a short digest of what is relevant to you, with links to read more.
tip: Schedule it for every morning and start the day informed.

title: Compare products before buying
chapter: Ch.17 Choosing tools without being fooled
scenario: You need new equipment and want an honest comparison of two models.
command: Compare these two printers for a small office: price, running cost and reliability.
caption: A side-by-side product comparison
result: The agent researches both products and lays out a clear comparison so you can pick the better fit for your budget and use.
tip: Ask for the total cost of ownership, not just the sticker price.

title: Plan a delivery route
scenario: You have several drops today and want a sensible route that saves driving time.
command: Plan the best route for these five delivery addresses and show it on a map.
caption: A delivery route mapped across the stops
result: The agent plots the stops on a map in an efficient order and gives you the distance and estimated time. You follow the route and save fuel.
tip: Add time windows ('stop B before noon') and the agent factors them in.

title: Where should I open next?
scenario: You are choosing a shop location and want to think about the area around each option.
command: Show these two candidate shop locations on a map and note what is near each one.
caption: Two candidate locations shown on a map
result: The agent maps both spots and notes nearby features — foot traffic, competitors, parking — to help you weigh the choice.
tip: Combine this with a web-research step on the neighbourhood for a fuller picture.

title: Draw your service area
scenario: You want to show customers the area you cover, so there is no confusion about delivery.
command: Show our service area on a map with the main towns we cover.
caption: A service-area map for customers
result: The agent produces a clear map of your coverage that you can put on your website or send to customers.
tip: Keep it updated as you grow — just ask for a new version.

title: Check an order in your system
chapter: Ch.19 Connecting AI to systems you already use
scenario: A customer asks where their order is. Instead of clicking through your ERP, you ask the agent.
command: What is the status of order 4821?
caption: An order status pulled from the business system
result: The agent looks up the order in your connected system and tells you its status in plain words — no menu hunting.
tip: This works once your business system is connected. See the book's connecting chapter.

title: Find a customer fast
scenario: On the phone, you need a customer's details quickly.
command: Find the customer Maria Rossi and show her contact and last order.
caption: A customer record retrieved on request
result: The agent finds the customer and shows the contact details and the last order, so you can help without putting them on hold.
tip: Ask for the last three orders if you want the full picture.

title: Is it in stock?
scenario: A customer wants to know if an item is available right now.
command: Do we have item SKU 3391 in stock, and how many?
caption: A live stock check answered in seconds
result: The agent checks the stock in your system and answers with the quantity, so you can promise or promise-against with confidence.
tip: Pair with a low-stock alert scheduled daily to avoid surprises.

title: Design a simple part
scenario: You need a simple bracket or part and do not want to open a heavy CAD program from scratch.
command: Design a small metal bracket 80 by 40 millimetres with four mounting holes.
caption: A simple part modelled through the CAD tool
result: The agent drives the CAD tool to model the part with the right dimensions, and you get a file you can review or export.
tip: Describe the shape and the measurements; the agent handles the CAD steps.

title: Check how parts fit
scenario: You want to see if two parts fit together before making them.
command: Place these two parts together and check for any overlap or clearance issues.
caption: An assembly check between two parts
result: The agent assembles the parts in the CAD model and points out where they clash or where the fit is too tight.
tip: Catch fit problems on screen, not on the workshop bench.

title: A drawing for the workshop
scenario: The workshop needs a drawing with dimensions to make the part.
command: Produce a technical drawing of the bracket with the key dimensions marked.
caption: A dimensioned technical drawing for production
result: The agent generates a drawing with the dimensions marked, ready for the person who will make the part.
tip: Ask for the view you need — top, side — so the drawing is clear.

title: Turn a topic into a podcast
scenario: You want a short audio piece for your audience — an interview-style episode on a topic you know.
command: Create a 5-minute podcast episode about why small shops should go online, in a friendly two-voice style.
caption: A podcast episode ready to play
result: The agent writes the script and produces an audio episode with two voices, ready to publish. Your message, in audio form, with no studio.
tip: Give it your key points and it shapes them into a natural conversation.

title: A briefing you can listen to
scenario: You would rather listen to the weekly update than read it. Turn the report into audio.
command: Turn this week's summary into a short audio briefing I can listen to on the way to work.
caption: An audio briefing ready to play
result: The agent converts the written summary into a clear audio briefing, so your commute becomes useful time.
tip: Schedule the weekly summary and its audio version together.

title: A report that writes itself each morning
chapter: Ch.11 Scheduled tasks (new chapter after ch.11)
scenario: You want the same report every morning without remembering to ask for it.
command: Every weekday at 8am, give me a summary of yesterday's sales and any urgent emails.
caption: A scheduled task set up to run each morning
result: The agent runs the report on its own each morning and has it waiting for you. You agreed the time once; it never forgets.
recurring: This is a recurring task. AgentBridge starts it at the agreed time and delivers the result to your chat, your email or your phone.
tip: You can change or stop a scheduled task any time by telling the agent.

title: Your week, wrapped up automatically
chapter: Ch.11 Scheduled tasks (new chapter after ch.11)
scenario: Every Friday you want a wrap-up of the week's numbers and what is due next.
command: Every Friday at 5pm, summarise this week's sales and list what is due next week.
caption: A weekly wrap-up scheduled to run every Friday
result: The agent prepares the weekly wrap-up automatically and sends it before you leave. Next week starts with a clear plan.
recurring: A weekly recurring task. AgentBridge handles the timing so you handle the decisions.

title: Never miss a deadline
chapter: Ch.11 Scheduled tasks (new chapter after ch.11)
scenario: A bill is due every month and you keep almost forgetting it.
command: Remind me on the 25th of every month that the supplier invoice is due.
caption: A recurring reminder set for a monthly deadline
result: The agent reminds you on the day, every month. You set it once and stop worrying about the date.
recurring: A monthly recurring reminder, delivered however you like — chat, email or phone.

title: Watch a page for changes
chapter: Ch.11 Scheduled tasks (new chapter after ch.11)
scenario: You want to know when a competitor changes their price, without checking by hand.
command: Check this competitor's pricing page every day and tell me if anything changes.
caption: A daily watch that alerts you to changes
result: The agent checks the page on schedule and only messages you when something actually changed. No noise, just the news.
recurring: A daily scheduled watch. It runs alone and reports only when there is something to report.

title: Speak instead of type
chapter: Ch.8 Voice and phone access (new chapter)
scenario: You have an idea while your hands are busy. You speak it and the agent writes it down.
command: (speak) Take a note: call the supplier about the delayed shipment tomorrow morning.
caption: A spoken note captured by the agent
result: The agent listens and writes the note for you. Your hands stay free; the thought is saved.
tip: Dictation works for messages, notes and even whole emails — just talk.

title: Let the agent read it to you
chapter: Ch.8 Voice and phone access (new chapter)
scenario: You would rather hear the answer than read a long message.
command: Read me the summary of today's orders out loud.
caption: The agent speaking its answer aloud
result: The agent reads the answer in a clear voice. Useful when you are moving, cooking, or your eyes are tired.
tip: You can ask for any answer to be spoken, not just summaries.

title: Call your assistant on the phone
chapter: Ch.8 Voice and phone access (new chapter)
scenario: You are out and need your assistant. You call a number and talk to it like a person.
command: (phone) What did I agree to deliver to the cafe this week?
caption: A phone call to your AgentBridge assistant
result: You call in, say what you need, and the agent answers from your notes and documents — by voice, wherever you are.
tip: Phone access is protected by a PIN, so only you can reach your assistant.

title: Hands-free on the road
chapter: Ch.8 Voice and phone access (new chapter)
scenario: You are driving and remember something you need from the office. You call and ask, hands-free.
command: (phone) Read me my appointment list for today.
caption: A hands-free call to check your day
result: The agent reads your appointments over the phone so you stay focused on the road and still have your day in hand.
tip: Keep calls short and focused while driving; save the long work for later.

title: Your assistant in Telegram
scenario: You already live in Telegram. Your assistant joins you there, so you ask things the same way.
command: (telegram) How much did we sell yesterday?
caption: A conversation with the agent inside Telegram
result: The agent answers in your Telegram chat, just like a colleague. Ask a question, get the answer, keep moving.
tip: Telegram access uses an allow-list, so only the people you choose can talk to it.

title: Get a document on your phone
scenario: You asked for a report at your desk and want it on your phone now.
command: (telegram) Send me the invoice you made for Bright Cafe.
caption: A document delivered into the Telegram chat
result: The agent sends the file into your Telegram chat. Open it, forward it, or download it — right from your phone.
tip: You can ask for any document you made earlier and have it sent to you.

title: The assistant in your team group
scenario: Your team has a group chat. Adding the agent means everyone can ask it things.
command: (telegram group) What are today's delivery stops?
caption: The agent answering in a team group chat
result: The agent joins the group and answers the team's questions with the shared information, so nobody has to be the walking encyclopedia.
tip: You control who is allowed in the group and what the agent may share.

title: Ask questions about your own files
scenario: Your answers are inside your own files. You ask a question and the agent finds it in your documents.
command: What is our cancellation policy with the printing supplier?
caption: The agent answering from your own documents
result: The agent searches your documents area and answers with what your own files actually say, pointing to the source.
tip: Keep your business files in the documents area and they become searchable knowledge.

title: Find that old document
scenario: You know you wrote something about this last year but cannot find the file.
command: Find the proposal I sent to the hotel last spring about the lobby redesign.
caption: A search through your indexed archive
result: The agent searches your indexed archive and brings back the document you meant, even when you only half-remember it.
tip: The index updates as you add files, so the archive is always current.

title: It remembers how you like things
scenario: You told the agent once how you like your invoices. Next time, it just does it that way.
command: Make an invoice — you know how I like them.
caption: The agent applying your saved preferences
result: The agent remembers your style and settings from before and applies them without you repeating yourself.
tip: You can correct it any time; it updates what it remembers.

title: Nothing is ever lost
scenario: You changed a document and want the earlier version back.
command: Show me the previous version of the contract and restore it.
caption: Version history lets you go back safely
result: Every version the agent made is kept. You can see the earlier draft and bring it back, so editing is always safe.
tip: This is why you can let the agent rewrite things freely — the history protects you.

title: The same assistant in your browser
chapter: Ch.19 Connecting AI to systems you already use
scenario: You prefer a browser window over the terminal. The same assistant is there, on any computer you own.
command: (browser) Draft a thank-you note to our regular customers.
caption: The AgentBridge web chat in a browser window
result: Open the web address and chat in the browser. Same tools, same documents, same memory — just a different window.
tip: Handy when you are on a different machine but still want your own assistant.

title: See all your agents at a glance
scenario: You run several agents and want one simple view of what each is doing.
command: (browser) Open the OfficeManager view.
caption: The OfficeManager view of your agents
result: OfficeManager shows your agents in one simple page, so you can see what is running and where things stand.
tip: A quick way to keep an eye on more than one assistant at once.

title: Plug it into your own tools
chapter: Ch.19 Connecting AI to systems you already use
scenario: You have a small app or script and want it to use the assistant. There is a simple web API for that.
command: POST /v1/chat/completions  { "model": "default-agent", "messages": [...] }
caption: The HTTP API lets other programs use the assistant
result: Your own programs can call the assistant through a standard web API, the same way they would call any online service. One integration, many uses.
tip: This is for the technical step — the book's connecting chapter walks through it.

title: Connect other AI tools to it
chapter: Ch.19 Connecting AI to systems you already use
scenario: You use other AI tools that speak the MCP standard. AgentBridge can act as their connector.
command: (MCP) Connect AgentBridge as a tool server.
caption: AgentBridge connected to other AI tools via MCP
result: Other AI applications can use AgentBridge's tools through the MCP standard, so your whole toolkit works together.
tip: MCP is for connecting tools; for everyday use the chat is all you need.
